label: copy-phase input m late in recall, mostly r-m-s contexts
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is m (100% of activations; in_first is always 0, so m is being re-read). Almost all activations (99% of mass) come at recall_idx >= 4, i.e. late in long sequences (65% of mass at L=9). It never fires on original or delimiter steps or on any other input token. Within copy-phase m it is sparse: only about 2% of late copy-phase m steps fire. Context raises the rate: the next output is s (43% of mass) or the previous input is r (36%). The exact trigram r m s with recall_idx >= 4 fires with 85% precision and gives the strongest activations (top example: ... r [m] s ...), but it covers only 10% of mass. Other next outputs that raise the rate are m, x, t, v and z. The recorded predicate (late copy-phase m with next output s or previous input r) gets dev F1 about 0.30 and mass recall 0.68. Most m steps in the same contexts stay silent, so the rest of what gates it is not captured by these variables.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=m (+5.36), prev_tok=r (+3.70), in_tok=m (+3.56), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+2.79), phase=2 & out_tok=x (+2.55), phase=2 & out_tok=t (+2.46). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.39), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.11), recall_idx=2 (-2.11), recall_idx=1 (-2.09).
